_comment: Manufacturing capability profile — the single source of truth for fab-driven layout decisions. Read by the layout tooling (layout_helpers.ModuleLayout). Hard geometric limits still live in each board's BoardConfig/DesignRules (DRC-enforced); this file is the *capabilities* layer (what the fab does cheaply).

via.note: JLC default plated via; smaller drills incur an upcharge

track_width_presets_mm.note: user track-width presets patched into every layout .kicad_pro so hand edits can pick real widths, not just the netclass width. Netclass width is the MINIMUM - prefer wider where space allows (manufacturing robustness).

via_in_pad.note: via-in-pad is fine when the pad's smaller dimension >= this (0402 and up). Below it (0201) a default-drill via won't sit in the pad without shrinking the hole below the free minimum, so route a short stub away and drop the via in open copper.

courtyard.note: House courtyard excess per side over union(pads, body) - IPC-7351 'Least' density, which is what a board packed to a 0.20-0.25mm pad-gap floor actually is. `placemat courtyard-audit` generates every footprint's F.CrtYd at this value, so DRC's courtyards_overlap fires at approximately the house floor and is a hard gate, not a margin warning. A courtyard is an ASSEMBLY KEEPOUT: no layout script may measure a board outline, envelope, pitch or edge placement through one (use placemat.layout_helpers.fp_phys_box_mm / fp_body_box_mm).

planes.note: Planes are a BOARD-level artifact drawn by hand. A module does NOT route distributed power/ground internally; it drops vias as landing points and the board plane feeds them.
